transcript:
Header: 2025-02-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Sophia Martinez (Acme Head of Partnerships), Liam O'Connor (Acme VP Sales), Evelyn Zhang (Acme AE)

Auto-summary: quick pipeline scrub, ask/ownership, action items.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan here from Redwood, I'll kick us off. how's everybody doing?
[00:08] Sophia Martinez: good, thanks. quick heads up, we're on a bit of a time check at 30 minutes for execs but we can go longer if needed.
[00:15] Jordan Lee: great, we'll prioritize deals. Priya, want to run through the pipeline doc?
[00:20] Priya Natarajan: sure. I pulled the joint sheet, there are three focus deals this quarter, I'll start with Deal A.
[00:27] Priya Natarajan: Deal A is a pilot for autonomous fleet optimization, Acme wants predictable latency and some edge deployment options. they asked about Dedicated vs Private.
[00:38] Liam O'Connor: yes, latency is the key. also they flagged cost as a constraint, like they want to keep per-token spend under a thresholds but need sub-100ms tail latency for inference.
[00:49] Jordan Lee: understood. on Dedicated we can guarantee throughput and have an SLA; on Private with VPC you'll get network isolation but setup time is longer.
[01:00] Sophia Martinez: timeline for Deal A is tight, they want pilot by end of Q1. is that feasible for Dedicated?
[01:07] Priya Natarajan: feasible if we provision reserved capacity, we can do a fast path for onboarding. we'll need a short integration test and a small perf benchmark.
[01:17] Evelyn Zhang: who will own the integration on Redwood side? we need one point of contact for the customer.
[01:22] Jordan Lee: Jordan will be owner for sales coordination, Priya will lead the technical integration and benchmarks. I'll tag that in the sheet.
[01:29] Liam O'Connor: ok. Deal B?
[01:31] Priya Natarajan: Deal B is a hosted API proof of concept for internal agent tooling, smaller scale but lots of eval criteria: output quality, hallucination rate, and cost per convo.
[01:44] Sophia Martinez: for Deal B they raised compliance questions - SSO, RBAC, and audit logs. are those part of the standard offering?
[01:52] Jordan Lee: yes, we support SAML SSO and RBAC through the console, and we expose audit logs. if they need SaaS-hosted logs retention beyond default we'll send a quote for extended retention.
[02:02] Priya Natarajan: also for sensitive data they can route through Private or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS. mention of KMS came up earlier.
[02:10] Liam O'Connor: cool. Deal C is the RFP for on-prem inference, big enterprise, long cycle. they want SOC2/ISO docs, and encryption at rest with HSM integration.
[02:21] Jordan Lee: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO artifacts, and support HSM/KMS integrations in Private. we'll send the security pack after the call.
[02:28] Sophia Martinez: perfect. can you include notes about data residency? some execs want to keep logs in EU.
[02:34] Priya Natarajan: yes we can route regionally; for Private you'd control region. for Dedicated we can provision in a European region to satisfy residency.
[02:44] Jordan Lee: quick note on competitors—Acme mentioned Anthropic and OpenAI in prior threads. any intel on their motions?
[02:52] Liam O'Connor: Anthropic is pushing safety claims and good product marketing; OpenAI is the default go-to but price is higher for low-latency dedicated setups.
[03:03] Priya Natarajan: from a technical standpoint we can differentiate on predictable tail latency and cost controls—batching, caching, quantization profiles.
[03:12] Evelyn Zhang: good point. can you run a side-by-side for us? sample prompts and latency/cost?
[03:18] Priya Natarajan: yes that's Priya action item, I'll run benchmarks on Acme prompt set and post results.
[03:22] Jordan Lee: Great. Next, co-sell roles: Sophia you and Liam will handle exec sponsor intros, Jordan will own Redwood side. we need a joint one-pager for Deal A to bring to the pilot stakeholders.
[03:34] Sophia Martinez: we'll draft the one-pager and send to Jordan by Friday.
[03:38] Liam O'Connor: also need to confirm billing model for pilot—will it be through Acme or passed through partner?
[03:44] Jordan Lee: for co-sell we typically bill the end customer directly; if Acme prefers partner-billed we can discuss partner arrangements. let's capture preferred flow per deal in the sheet.
[03:53] Sophia Martinez: noted.
[03:54] [04:00] -- (15 minute mark check-in) --
[04:05] Priya Natarajan: technical risks for Deal A: model size and sequence length; if they have long telemetry sequences we might need a quantized model or a split-encoder approach.
[04:15] Evelyn Zhang: there's also data retention for telemetry, they asked if we purge logs after 30 days.
[04:20] Jordan Lee: retention policies are configurable, we'll propose 30-day default and discuss stricter retention if needed.
[04:26] Liam O'Connor: can Redwood support per-route SLAs? some customers want higher SLAs for critical endpoints.
[04:32] Priya Natarajan: yes with Dedicated you can get tighter SLOs; we can add route-level monitoring and alerts in the Console.
[04:40] Sophia Martinez: ok. let's talk timing—given everyone's bandwidth, what's realistic for the pilot rollout steps?
[04:47] Jordan Lee: propose timeline: week 1-2 integration and initial test, week 3 perf benchmark and tuning, week 4 pilot validation with customer metrics. that's end of month if we start immediately.
[04:58] Liam O'Connor: need an exec sponsor intro before week 1 ideally.
[05:02] Jordan Lee: understood, Sophia will confirm.
[05:05] [06:00] -- small cross talk, background noise --
[06:10] Evelyn Zhang: quick question on pricing: is there a minimum commit for Dedicated?
[06:16] Jordan Lee: yes Dedicated typically has a reserved capacity commit; we offered a modest pilot commit for these situations, then scale based on telemetry. I'll follow up with pricing options.
[06:25] Priya Natarajan: another note: for Deal B if it's hosted we can instrument evals with internal prompt sets and send quality reports; that helps the buyer justify the TCO.
[06:36] Sophia Martinez: sounds good. on the RFP (Deal C) the security team will want legal templates and also proof of past deployments in regulated sectors.
[06:45] Jordan Lee: we can provide references and the legal playbook; I'll loop in legal after the call.
[06:50] Liam O'Connor: any blockers from Redwood side?
[06:53] Priya Natarajan: just need the sample prompts and a small telemetry dataset for accurate benchmarks.
[06:59] Jordan Lee: can Acme share that?
[07:02] Sophia Martinez: yes we'll share a sanitized sample by Thursday.
[07:07] Jordan Lee: perfect. final quick recap then next steps.
[07:12] Jordan Lee: recap: Jordan to update pipeline and tag owners; Priya to run benchmarks; Redwood to send security pack; Acme to confirm exec sponsor and provide sample data.
[07:24] Sophia Martinez: correct. we'll also prepare the one-pager and clarify billing flow per deal.
[07:30] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone. any other questions?
[07:34] Evelyn Zhang: none from me.
[07:36] Liam O'Connor: all good.
[07:38] Jordan Lee: ok we'll follow up in the sheet and book a follow-up next week. thanks everyone, bye.

Post-call notes: shared joint pipeline spreadsheet link (internal), security pack to be sent by Jordan, benchmark results expected from Priya, customer to provide exec sponsor and sanitized prompts.
